query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Doping a TiB₂-based boride component with ~2 wt % molybdenum (forming a (Ti,Mo)B₂ solid solution) will cut the dissolution/corrosion rate in molten Al by ≥50 % relative to undoped TiB₂ during hot-dip aluminum-plating operations.
generation.material_initial_state: Baseline dense TiB₂ ceramic typical of boride wear parts used in hot-dip Al-plating baths; grain size ≈5 µm; porosity <2 vol %.
generation.intervention: Introduce 2 wt % Mo powder during hot-press sintering to produce a homogeneous (Ti₀.₉₅Mo₀.₀₅)B₂ solid solution (no secondary metallic phase).
generation.conditions: Immersion in industrial-grade molten Al (≤1 wt % Mg, ≤0.3 wt % Si) at 700 ± 20 °C for up to 24 h; stagnant bath; ambient atmosphere; no significant flux additions.
generation.structural_mediator: Mo atoms substitute in the TiB₂ lattice and segregate to grain boundaries where they promote formation of a thin, continuous Mo-rich boride layer (likely MoB/Mo₂B) at the ceramic/Al interface.
generation.mechanism: The Mo-rich interfacial layer has (1) lower chemical solubility in molten Al and (2) a coefficient of thermal expansion closer to TiB₂, suppressing crack formation. Together these effects hinder direct dissolution of TiB₂ grains and block intermetallic (Al–Ti) penetration, thereby slowing corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Average mass-loss rate of Mo-doped samples will be ≤0.5 mg cm⁻² h⁻¹ versus ≥1 mg cm⁻² h⁻¹ for undoped TiB₂ under the stated conditions; cross-sectional SEM/EDS will show an interfacial Mo-rich boride layer ≤2 µm thick on doped samples but not on the baseline.
generation.baseline: Commercial hot-pressed TiB₂ with no intentional Mo addition, tested side-by-side in the same molten Al bath.
generation.boundary: The protective effect is expected to diminish above 850 °C or in Al baths containing >2 wt % Mg or aggressive fluxing agents that disrupt boride layers.
generation.uncertainty: No published data were located that directly measure molten-Al corrosion of (Ti,Mo)B₂; magnitude of benefit and layer stability beyond 24 h are therefore uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of coupons: (1) TiB₂ and (2) (Ti,Mo)B₂ (2 wt % Mo). Immerse paired coupons in the same crucible of molten Al at 700 °C for 8, 16, and 24 h. Record initial and final masses (after pickling in NaOH to remove adhering Al), and perform cross-sectional SEM/EDS of interfaces.
measurements: Mass loss per unit area (mg cm⁻²)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mo-doped samples do NOT show (a) ≥25 % lower mass-loss rate than undoped TiB₂ at any time point and (b) no distinct Mo-rich boride layer at the interface, the hypothesis is falsified.
